course_info.faculty: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences

catalog_course_description: This course introduces graduate students to major debates in political theory within the analytic tradition. It examines key questions about political values and concepts such as justice, equality, freedom, democracy, power, and authority. Emphasis is placed on critical engagement with theoretical texts and the development of conceptual and analytical skills for understanding and evaluating political institutions and practices.
course_learning_outcomes: Identify and explain major debates in contemporary political theory concerning central values and concepts, such as justice, equality, freedom, democracy, power and authority
Analyze and critically assess normative arguments in key theoretical texts
Articulate the implications of different normative frameworks for evaluating political institutions and practices
Develop a nuanced understanding of political concepts that play a central role in both normative theorizing and empirical political research
Engage in reasoned discussion and debate about contested political concepts
Develop and defend their own normative and conceptual positions in written form
